report:
Fresh source assessment of the complete owner_parameters claim. Requirements are reuse of the owning trait/impl Self and parameter identities, introduction of item parameters only after owner parameters, pairing Binder.value with its binding generics, and identity preservation when opening/copying. The ordinary fns.rs association implements owner opening: trait signatures supply their existing self_param and generic slice, impl signatures supply existing self_ty and generic slice, and no-owner functions receive an empty prefix. LocalFnSym::sig adds that owner scope before CheckGenerics and concatenates owner parameters before method parameters, recording owner_generic_count. Captured CheckGenerics creates only item parameters using the item parent identity. The ordinary ty.rs Binder association covers value plus generics storage and the StashCopy implementation for both fields. Captured Stashed::open returns the existing root; copy_into dispatches StashCopy; Slice copies its elements and GenericParam is StashDirect, whose copying returns the same identity. These paths do not remint owner identities.

Reviewed every associated test body. associated_items_reuse_owner_generics_and_bodies_resolve_fields asserts the impl owner, one generic, receiver Wrap identity, equality between the owner type argument and method return type, and a diagnostic-free resolved field body. trait_and_impl_signatures_share_complete_generic_binders asserts trait Self-plus-T and impl T binder lengths, eligible environments and identical tuple element types, providing supporting owner-binder shape evidence. trait_items_have_stable_symbols_and_owner_identity asserts trait item ownership and equality of the method generic slice with the trait-items binder, directly detecting replacement of trait Self identity; it also exercises receiverless associated functions. Setup helpers construct an in-memory crate and pass actual database/root objects to these visible assertions.

The remaining test entry, todo::types_binder_owner_parameters, explicitly defers direct copy/open identity checks and simultaneous owner-plus-method generic tests across all associated item kinds. It is not a behavioral test and supplies no passing coverage for those scenarios. Existing tests do not establish those complete scenarios; this limitation remains honestly visible. The implementation entry ty::todo separately defers alias/constant owner-opening behavior. Captured LocalTypeAliasSym and LocalConstSym currently carry owner identity and CST/attribute access but no checked signature queries; introducing those APIs is the stated prerequisite for their owner-preserving signature implementation and corresponding coverage. This is justified deferred scope, not implemented behavior or an N/A claim. Ordinary function/Binder implementation evidence remains intact. No new contradiction was found that requires a regression investigation.

This refresh executed review start/read/record commands only, changed no Rust source, and makes no new test-execution or build claim. Root coordinates current test suites. Current evidence supports approval with the explicit implementation and test TODOs remaining deferred; no further source edits requested.
